name: Bayesian Decision Networks
analogy: Think of it as a flowchart that understands doubt. Boxes for things you are unsure about are linked by arrows showing what influences what, a box marks the choice you control, and a final box scores the outcome. Feed in what you have seen, and the chart tells you which choice has the best expected score.

steps.title: Draw the uncertain things and how they connect
steps.description: Each uncertain quantity gets a node. An arrow from one node to another means the first influences the second. Each node carries a small table of probabilities given its parents.
steps.inExample: A node for the volatility regime (calm or elevated) points to a node for tomorrow's average true range being high or low.

steps.title: Add the decision and the score
steps.description: A decision node lists the choices you control, and a utility node says how good each combination of choice and outcome is. This turns a probability model into a decision tool.
steps.inExample: The decision is how much of a 10-contract MNQ long to hedge: none, half or all. The score is the risk-adjusted profit in US dollars.

steps.title: Enter what you have observed
steps.description: Observed nodes are fixed at their known values. The beliefs about every unobserved node are updated using the probability tables, working backwards from the evidence to the cause.
steps.inExample: The average true range today is high. Before the evidence, the chance of an elevated regime was 30 percent. After it, the chance is 63 percent.

steps.title: Score every choice under the updated beliefs
steps.description: For each possible choice, the model weighs the score in each outcome by the probability of that outcome. The result is an expected score for each choice.
steps.inExample: With elevated at 63 percent and calm at 37 percent, the expected score is minus 475 for no hedge, minus 135 for half, and minus 149 for a full hedge.

steps.title: Pick the best choice and report the reasoning
steps.description: The choice with the highest expected score is recommended. The updated probabilities at every node can be inspected, so the reasoning is open to checking.
steps.inExample: The recommendation is the half hedge, because it protects well in the elevated regime without giving up too much in the calm one.

useFor.example: Choosing a hedge ratio for a long MNQ position when it is unclear whether volatility is entering an elevated regime.
Selecting a position size by expected score after a penalty for large losses, instead of by expected return alone.
Letting news sentiment, volatility and a trend signal each update the belief about tomorrow's regime before a decision.
Stating when switching off an automated risk limit would be justified by the evidence at hand.

avoidWhen: The decision unfolds over many bars and today's choice changes tomorrow's situation; a dynamic version that links time steps handles that.
You have no sound way to estimate the probability tables; the answer would reflect your guesses rather than the data.

example.scenario: A trader is long 10 MNQ contracts and sees an unusually high average true range today. They want to know whether to hedge none, half or all of the position, given a prior belief that the market is entering an elevated-volatility regime.

input.summary: The prior belief, how the evidence relates to the regime, and the scores of each choice in each regime.

fields.name: prior chance of an elevated regime
fields.meaning: The belief before seeing today's range.

fields.name: chance of a high range if elevated
fields.meaning: How often an elevated regime shows a high average true range.

fields.name: chance of a high range if calm
fields.meaning: How often a calm regime still shows a high average true range.

fields.name: evidence observed
fields.meaning: The fact that is entered into the network today.

fields.name: no hedge score
fields.value: minus 900 if elevated, plus 250 if calm
fields.meaning: Risk-adjusted result in US dollars of holding the full position.

fields.name: half hedge score
fields.value: minus 250 if elevated, plus 60 if calm

fields.name: full hedge score
fields.value: minus 60 if elevated, minus 300 if calm
fields.meaning: Risk-adjusted result of hedging all, including the cost of giving up the upside.

output.summary: The updated belief, the expected score of each choice and the recommendation.

fields.name: updated chance of an elevated regime
fields.meaning: The belief after the high range is taken into account.

fields.name: expected score with no hedge
fields.meaning: Probability-weighted score of holding the full position.

fields.name: recommended choice
fields.meaning: The choice with the best expected score.

example.reading: The half hedge wins narrowly over the full hedge, so a small change in the probability tables could change the answer. Check how sensitive the choice is to the 80 and 20 percent figures before acting on it.
